trickyParts: A generated Go SDK refuses a nil required Input in its constructor before the plugin is ever called, so the thirteen Dispatch inputs had to become optional in the schema for a cluster-only program to compile at all. Nothing on the provider side enforces required-ness, so the resolver is what keeps them required while clusterOnly is off; the schema test and the refusal table together are what hold that.

The five outputs Dispatch would decide are set to an explicit pulumi.String("").ToStringOutput(). A field left unset awaits as unknown, which is one value in preview and another in update; agent-infra's legion/ program already reads an empty databaseInstance as 'dispatch/ has not been applied'.
newDispatchCluster had to keep the project lookup and the network so the database half could build on them without a second organizations.LookupProjectOutput invoke.

The 46-row refusal table is held complete by a reflection test over DispatchArgs' pulumi tags, so an input added later is either deliberately live or refused, and cannot reach a cluster-only component in silence.
deviations: The registration golden is sorted, not in registration order, which the plan's task 1 asked for. The Pulumi Go SDK registers each resource from a goroutine of its own, so the order the mock engine records is the scheduler's: measured on this branch's base, three runs of the same program produced three different orders, and a golden captured from one run failed ten of ten later runs. The golden still pins every resource, its name and its parent, which is what the plan wanted it for.
The cluster-only mock-engine tests live in a new file, gcp/dispatch_cluster_only_test.go, rather than in gcp/dispatch_test.go as the plan's task 6 named: that file is already 2,477 lines.
The dispatchKubernetes struct is gone. Its only field was the kubeconfig, which the cluster half now computes and NewDispatch reads from dispatchCluster, so newDispatchKubernetes returns error alone.

The spec departures the architect accepted stand: the live preview of agent-infra's dispatch/ stack is dispatch://INFRA-775's (agent-infra pins envoy-infra@2.9.1 while this repository's newest release is envoy-infra-v5.4.0, so no stack runs this code), and the release this cuts is the major envoy-infra-v6.0.0.
discoveredComplexity: The three acceptance commands the plan names cannot be run as one package run in a worker pod: gcp/data_disk_test.go needs mkfs.ext4 and blkid, which the image does not carry and uid 1000 cannot install, and those tests fail rather than skip. The filtered runs this handoff names are what a pod can run; CI's envoy-infra-go job covers the rest.

go test -tags natslive ./core/ ./seed/, one of that job's four commands, cannot run in a worker pod either: its live tests start NATS through testcontainers and the pod has no Docker daemon (panic: rootless Docker not found). Both failures are environmental and untouched by this change.
pulumi package gen-sdk over the whole plugin takes about five and a half minutes; the whole SDK smoke, download to compiled consumer, is about nine minutes.
